cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's Audit Machine test the payroll of HANGS Construction Services.
It ties the payroll ledger to the books, to the cent.
Materiality, the size of error that matters, is $340,000.
Every month lands within about four percent of its expectation.
Next it rebuilds eight sample paychecks from their timesheets and pay rates.
One insurance deduction runs a little high on overtime.
The payroll manager entered her own raise, with no signed approval.
Now it ties payroll to the books and to all four quarterly payroll tax returns.
But about $23,000 of employer payroll tax for June was never recorded in June.
Now it adds up what it found and sets it against materiality.
Then it writes the workpapers and a draft findings memo for the CPA.

All done. Known errors add up to just over $25,000, well under materiality, including about $2,500 owed back to the crews. The bigger issue is control: the unapproved raise. Seven items stay open. The CPA, a person, concludes and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
